t: Karim Khan Zand restored order to most of Iran after Nader Shah's murder, ruling from Shiraz without ever taking the title of shah.
His mild rule revived trade and farming and left Shiraz its Vakil bazaar, mosque and bath, still among Iran's finest 18th-century buildings.
After his death in 1779 his relatives fought for the throne, and the Qajar Agha Mohammad Khan destroyed the dynasty by 1794.
dyk: Karim Khan called himself Vakil al-Ruaya, Deputy of the People, rather than shah, and kept a Safavid prince as nominal sovereign.
ev: Nader Shah's assassination leaves Iran in a power vacuum
Karim Khan Zand and Ali Mardan Khan install the puppet Shah Ismail III
Karim Khan lets the British East India Company open a factory at Bushehr
Karim Khan restores the tomb of the poet Hafez in Shiraz
Sadeq Khan's forces capture Basra from the Ottomans after a long siege
Karim Khan dies, opening fifteen years of Zand civil war
Shiraz's governor betrays the city to the Qajars
Agha Mohammad Khan takes Kerman and executes the last Zand ruler, Lotf Ali Khan
